chapter_theme: Kiriyai (கிரியை), worship of the Lord by rite and service: refuge at the feet of the one God of all directions frees from the sea of deeds, but rich offerings reach him only from those who have given up flesh. Service done by humans is service to the Lord, and kiriyai with chariyai leads on through yoga and jnana, by the guru's grace, to becoming Siva.
structure_note: Refuge at the feet (1451), the condition of not eating flesh (1452), an obscure verse of praise built on கன்று (1453), service as devotion (1454), the ladder from kiriyai to Siva (1455) and a first-person close of love and service (1456).

1451.reading: In all ten directions there is one supreme God, and there is no direction where he is not; take refuge in the shade of the Pure One's holy feet, clustered like flowers, and the leaping sea of deeds will not reach you.
1451.nuance: கொத்து (a cluster, of flowers) pictures the feet as a bunch of blossoms; the shade (நீழல்) is the refuge. தத்தும் (leaping, surging) makes வினை a sea with waves. எத்திக்கு இலர் இல்லை may also mean 'there is no one in any direction who is without him'.

1452.reading: Even if one worships with crores of fragrant forest sandal and great flowers that reach the sky, none but those who eat having put away flesh can reach his flower-anklets where the honey sits.
1452.nuance: The verse sets the scale of offering against one abstention. ஊனினை நீக்கி may also be taken as 'removing the body', but in a chapter on worship and with உண்பவர் (those who eat) it reads most naturally as giving up meat.

1453.reading: Praise his sounding anklets as the king's calf; the Lord, calf of jnana who roams in the middle, calf of the sky whom the gods worship with joined hands, and holder of the deer's calf, is a vessel of grace.
1453.nuance: Each line turns on கன்று (calf, young one): கோனக்கன்று, ஞானக்கன்று, வானக்கன்று, மானக்கன்று. Only the last is clear, the deer Siva holds in his hand. Whether the worshipper or the Lord is the calf in line 1, and what நடுவே உழிதரும் (roams in the middle) refers to, I can't fix. வள்ளம் may be a vessel, a boat or a measure.

1454.reading: Bow to this: she who serves all the regions of the eight directions is a part of him; the service humans do is service to the Lord; serving the Lord is devotion.
1454.nuance: அவள் ஒரு கூறன் is the Lord who has her (Shakti) as half his body. The words இது, அது and பணி are repeated so densely that the grammar is unclear; பதிபணி may be service to the Lord (பதி) or service at his shrine.

1455.reading: The devotee, practising kiriyai and chariyai, moves by pure grace into flawless yoga, and through the jnana realised on the path it leads to, by the guru's grace, the mind becomes Siva.
1455.nuance: The verse gives the whole ladder in one sentence: chariyai and kiriyai, then yoga, then jnana, then Sivam. Each step is credited to grace (சுத்த அருள், குருவருள்), not only to practice. It names kiriyai before chariyai, perhaps for metre.

1456.reading: Melting in love, I serve him every day; standing before his body of red gold and his lotus feet, I ask him to grant me words to speak there, and he shines as a light within my bones.
1456.nuance: The grammar of lines 2 and 3 is loose: மொழிவது எனக்கருள் may be 'grant me what to say' or 'grant me grace, I say'. என்பினுள் சோதி, the light within the bone, answers the image of bones melting in love (compare 272).

links.note: Both make the Lord's feet the only crossing of a sea: the Kural's great sea of births, Tirumular's leaping sea of deeds. Reaching the feet is the condition in both.
Both set one abstention above a mass of offerings: the Kural puts not killing and eating above a thousand fire sacrifices, Tirumular puts giving up flesh above crores of sandal and flowers.
199 threatens meat-eaters with hell; 1452 adds that their worship, however rich, does not reach the Lord's feet.
272 says even burning one's bones as firewood wins nothing without melting in love; in 1456 the devotee melts in love and the Lord shines within the bones.

Tirumanthiram 1451 says that for one who takes the shade of the Pure One's feet as refuge (திருவடி நீழல் சரண்), the surging sea of deeds (தத்தும் வினைக்கடல்) will not reach him. Kural 7 says that only those who reach the feet of the incomparable one (தனக்குவமை இல்லாதான் தாள் சேர்ந்தார்க்கு) can remove the mind's anxiety. Both make reaching the feet the single way out; the Kural names inner care, Tirumular the force of karma.

Tirumanthiram 1454, in dense wordplay on பணி, seems to say that the service humans do (மானுடர் செய்பணி) is service to the Lord (ஈசன் பதிபணி). Tirumanthiram 1857 says plainly that what is given to the 'walking temple' (நடமாடக் கோயில்) reaches the god of the temple of images (படமாடக் கோயில்). If 1454 is read so, 1857 is its clear statement; the link depends on that uncertain reading of 1454.

Tirumanthiram 1455 makes chariyai and kiriyai, then yoga, then jnana, a ladder by which the devotee's mind becomes Siva (சித்தம் ... சிவமாகுமே), each step carried by grace. Thiruppugazh 643 asks for the reality that is hard to reach (எட்டரிதாய) for those of chariyai, kiriyai and yoga. On the reading that the song sets those paths aside as unable to reach the goal, it conflicts with 1455's claim that they lead to it; if it only means they fall short on their own, the two agree.

source_issues: 1453: lines 1 and 2 (கோனக்கன் றாயே, நடுவே யுழிதரும்) are obscure and may be corrupt.
